dedupe_keys.name: sicobiona open source pedestrian evacuation simulator based on the social force model

description: SiCoBioNa is an open-source simulator of pedestrian evacuation from enclosed spaces based on the Social Force Model, described in a December 2025 preprint by López, Mazzone, Rubio Puzzo and Moreno. The model represents goal-oriented motion of each pedestrian, interactions between people and interactions with walls and obstacles. A graphical interface lets users configure pedestrian properties, room and exit geometries and initial conditions without expertise in numerical methods, and the simulator produces quantitative outputs such as evacuation times together with visualisations, so that different spatial layouts can be compared. Its design is modular and extensible and aimed at reproducible research on pedestrian dynamics and at practical evacuation planning. Coverage is any enclosed space the user draws. The preprint is free and available on arXiv and states that the software is open source. Caveats: it models pedestrians only, without smoke, fire or vehicles, calibration against real evacuations is limited, and the tool is new and not peer reviewed. Simulation uses: estimating evacuation times for hospitals, shelters and public buildings, testing exit layouts, and feeding building evacuation times into wider emergency response models. Related records: the Stockholm hospital evacuation exercises (case_study-region-stockholm-hospital-evacuation-simulation-exercises) and the Louisiana hospital evacuation planning case study (case_study-louisiana-hospital-air-evacuation-simulation) address evacuation of health facilities.
